subject: ParcelLogic — Dedicated GPU sizing: follow-up & questionnaire
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@parcellogic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ParcelLogic — Dedicated GPU sizing: follow-up & questionnaire

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about ParcelLogic's roadmap for generative parcel routing. To make sure we size a Dedicated pool that meets your latency and cost goals, can you take 10–15 minutes to answer the checklist below (high level is fine to start):

1) Traffic profile
   - Typical QPS by endpoint (inbound API calls per second) and any known daily/weekly peaks
   - Percent of traffic that is conversational (multi-turn) vs single-shot inference

2) Concurrency & sessions
   - Average concurrent sessions/persistent sessions vs peak concurrent requests
   - Typical session lifetime (median / 95th percentile in seconds)

3) Prompt & response lengths
   - Distribution (or averages) of prompt tokens and response tokens; approximate 50/90/99th percentiles if available
   - Percent of requests that use streaming vs full-response at once

4) Latency & SLOs
   - P50/P95 target latency (token or response-level), and any hard p99 requirement for customer-facing flows

5) Workload variability
   - Are there predictable bursts (time-of-day / day-of-week) or ad-hoc spikes (e.g., campaign launches)?

6) Data residency & compliance constraints
   - Any region restrictions or encryption/KMS requirements we should account for in Private/Dedicated deployments

If you can, please attach a 24–72h sample of request-level telemetry (CSV or JSON) with timestamp, endpoint, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, and status. We can run that through our sizing probes and produce a recommended GPU mix (i.e., A100_vs_H100, quantization tradeoffs, estimated cost per 1M tokens).

Proposed next step: once we have the sample telemetry, we can run a 60–90 minute sizing workshop with engineering + platform (we'll bring Marissa and Ben). Availability from our side: next Wed/Thu morning PST. Does that work?

Thanks — short answers are totally fine.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
--
Attachment stub: request_sample_template.csv (CSV header with timestamp,endpoint,prompt_tokens,response_tokens,status)

From: Asha Rao <asha@parcellogic.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Parcello Platform Team <infra@parcellogic.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ParcelLogic — Dedicated GPU sizing: follow-up & questionnaire

Hi Grace — thanks, this is great. Quick answers below and I've attached a 48h sample export and a few example payloads.

1) Traffic profile
   - Baseline: 18 qps across our primary "routing" endpoint (POST /v1/routing)
   - Peak observed during business hours: 120 qps (we also see spikes to ~200 qps during promotional surges)
   - Conversational vs single shot: ~72% single-shot (one-off route calc), ~28% multi-turn session where an operator follows up (conversations average 3 turns)

2) Concurrency & sessions
   - Average concurrent requests: ~45
   - Peak concurrent: ~260 (corresponds to promo spikes)
   - Session lifetime: median ~40s, 95th ~310s

3) Prompt & response lengths
   - Prompt tokens: median 120, p90 510, p99 2,200
   - Response tokens: median 45, p90 260, p99 1,100
   - Streaming: ~30% streaming for longer responses (analytics/route tracebacks)

4) Latency & SLOs
   - Target: P95 end-to-end response < 350ms for single-shot; p99 soft target 900ms. Conversational flows can accept higher p99 up to ~1.8s for backend processing tasks.

5) Workload variability
   - Predictable weekdays 08:00–18:00 local time heavy, campaign spikes unpredictable but last ~10–40 minutes.

6) Data residency & compliance
   - Must keep customer data in us-west region; SOC2 compliant storage preferred.

Attachments: parcellogic_token_histogram.csv, sample_payloads.json

We'd like the workshop — Thu morning PST works best for our engineering lead. Also looping infra (infra@parcellogic.com) to confirm any network/VPC constraints.

—Asha
Asha Rao
Head of Platform, ParcelLogic
asha@parcellogic.com
--
Attachment stubs: parcellogic_token_histogram.csv, sample_payloads.json

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@parcellogic.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ParcelLogic — Dedicated GPU sizing: follow-up & questionnaire

Thanks Asha — these numbers are very helpful. Quick clarifying questions before we run the sizing probe:

- The attached CSV looks like request-level rows but I noticed a handful of anonymized internal IDs in the endpoint column. Can you confirm that each row is a single inference request (i.e., prompt_tokens + response_tokens represent one request) and not aggregated batches?
- For the promotional spikes: are they typically bursty (many short requests) or sustained (elevated qps for several hours)? That changes our recommendation on queuing vs reserved burst capacity.
- Do you have a list of "critical" customer-facing endpoints that require the tighter p99 SLA? We can tier those onto higher-priority queues/favored model variants.

Workshop logistics: Thu 12 Nov 2026, 09:30–11:00 PST works for our team (Grace + me + Ben). We'll prepare:
  - a sizing run on your 48h telemetry (we'll produce GPU mix + estimated peak occupancy)
  - a draft deployment topology (reserved pool + burst path + fallback smaller model)
  - high-level cost estimate for 3,6,12 month committed tiers

Ben, can you bring a sample pricing worksheet and a note on commitment thresholds we usually recommend for this profile?

Asha — please confirm the time and whether infra@parcellogic.com can provide temporary read-only access to the telemetry CSV in Drive or share a signed S3 presigned link.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Asha Rao <asha@parcellogic.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Parcello Platform Team <infra@parcellogic.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ParcelLogic — Dedicated GPU sizing: follow-up & questionnaire

Confirmed — Thu 12 Nov, 09:30 PST is good.

Answers inline:
- CSV rows are single requests (not pre-aggregated). infra@parcellogic.com will create a read-only Drive folder and drop the raw export and a presigned S3 link for the full 7-day window.
- Promo spikes are short and bursty (10–45 minutes), primarily many short requests rather than long sessions.
- Critical endpoints: POST /v1/routing and POST /v1/manifest-validate (both user-facing). Internal analytics endpoints can tolerate higher latency.

Notes on compliance: we host data in us-west and are SOC2 in-scope; we will not be able to export customer-identifiable logs outside of the us-west region without a DPA addendum. I'll attach our SOC2 scope summary during the workshop.

Thanks — looking forward to the sizing run.

Asha
(added infra contact to the thread)
